newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian privatisation raised 2.3 bln pounds in 96.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian privatisation raised 2.3 bln pounds in 96.

text.p: The Egyptian government raised 2.3 billion pounds ($680million) in 1996 through the sale of assets under its privatisation programme, the minister in charge of the programme said in remarks published on Monday.

The government has used 80 percent of this revenue to pay off the debts of other public-sector companies in preparation for privatisation, Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid told the government newspaper al-Ahram.

In 1996 the state relinquished majority control of 16 companies and sold between 10 and 40 percent of its stake in nine others which the government wants to control for social reasons, it quoted him as saying.

Obeid said the programme for 1997 was to sell off shares in 52 companies -- 12 to small investors through the stock exchange and 40 by sale to anchor investors. Two days ago Obeid was quoted as saying the 1997 target would be 51 companies.
If Egypt could not find anchor investors it would look at alternatives such as leasing and management contracts.
